descriptionChirho: Pertaining to or proceeding from the Holy Spirit; of the nature of spirit as opposed to flesh or the material order. Used attributively to modify nouns: spiritual gifts (1 Cor 12:1; 14:1), spiritual body (1 Cor 15:44,46), spiritual food and drink (1 Cor 10:3-4), spiritual songs (Eph 5:19; Col 3:16), spiritual blessing (Eph 1:3). Translations render adjectivally: eng 'spiritual,' spa 'espiritual/espirituales,' arb روحِيَّةٍ/روحِيٌّ (ruhiyyah, of the spirit), hin आत्मिक (aatmik, spiritual), kor 영적인/신령한 (yeongjeok-in/sinryeonghan, of spirit), swa 'kiroho' (spiritual).

Spiritual realities, blessings, or matters treated as a substantive noun; the things that pertain to the Spirit. Used when the adjective stands alone as a noun phrase meaning 'spiritual things/matters' (1 Cor 2:13; 9:11; 14:37; cf. Rom 15:27). Translations shift to nominalized forms: eng 'spiritual things,' spa 'espirituales cosas' (spiritual matters), arb الرُّوحِيَّاتِ (ar-ruhiyyaat, the spiritual realities), hin आत्मिक बातों में (aatmik baaton men, in spiritual matters), kor 영적인 것들 (yeongjeok-in geotdeul, spiritual things), swa 'vya kiroho' (matters of spirit). This substantival use parallels τὰ σαρκικά in Paul's rhetoric.
